artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $F$ be a finite field, and call a set $A \subseteq F \times F \times F$ a Besicovitch (Kakeya) set if for every direction $v \in F^3 \setminus \{0\}$ there exists $x \in F^3$ such that the line $\{x + tv : t \in F\}$ is contained in $A$. It is known that any such set satisfies $|A| \gtrsim |F|^{5/2}$. Prove that there exists an absolute constant $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every Besicovitch set $A \subseteq F^3$ satisfies $|A| \gtrsim |F|^{5/2 + \varepsilon}$.
artifact.status_search_result: In 2008, Z. Dvir resolved the finite field Kakeya conjecture in full generality using the polynomial method, proving that any Kakeya set in F^n has size at least c_n |F|^n. In particular, for n=3 this gives |A| ≳ |F|^3, vastly exceeding the |F|^{5/2+ε} bound requested, and thus settles the problem.

status_evidence.title: On the size of Kakeya sets in finite fields
status_evidence.snippet: Dvir proves that any Kakeya set in F^n has at least c_n |F|^n elements.
status_evidence.claim: The finite field Kakeya conjecture, which implies the requested improvement, is fully solved.

status_evidence.title: Dvir's proof of the finite field Kakeya conjecture (Tao blog)
status_evidence.snippet: Dvir's short polynomial-method proof shows |K| ≥ c_n |F|^n for any Kakeya set K ⊆ F^n.
